A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReGATE research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original ReGATE benchmark evaluations and training-efficiency measurements in Tables 1–4, plus weighting-factor and teacher-capacity ablations in Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v3 retains those original evaluations and ablations and adds token-selection examples with reference losses, student EMA losses, and retention outcomes in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The reference-plus-EMA scoring, top-k gating, sparsity schedule, and sparse attention/MLP procedure are unchanged. Expanded Section 3.4 incorporates Algorithm 1 and Q/K/V masking information already present in v2 supplementary Section 6. Adaptive scheduling remains future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets and subsets, five image benchmarks, and eight video benchmarks. Figure 6 adds illustrative video-QA cases without establishing additional task, domain, or evaluation-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and in the LaVi and LLaVA-Meteor comparisons in Tables 5–6. The teacher-capacity alternatives in Table 8 are also retained.

E3.justification: The stated model configurations, training budgets, metrics, 16-frame evaluations, and Table 9 prompts are unchanged. Both retain C=128, F=16, p_sparse=0.5, and the 100-iteration warm-up; Figure 6 also specifies p=0.5 rather than a revised protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds two token-selection failure examples in Figure 6, examining whether fixed 50% retention can exclude useful answer tokens. The weighting-factor and teacher-capacity ablations, attention visualizations, and earlier reference-loss examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The additional token-loss values are diagnostic measurements rather than statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and Figures 3–5 retain their results. Figure 6 adds token losses and retention outcomes, including 'static' marked skipped with total loss 13.06. Its caption also calls 'NASA' skipped, although the figure marks NASA green as retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the EMA/reference-score formulation, and the top-k mask definitions are unchanged. No mathematical theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims remain parameter-free, architecture-compatible training acceleration, up to 2× faster matching of baseline MVBench accuracy using 38% of tokens, and improved results with extended training. The expanded contribution bullet makes previously reported full-parameter and LoRA applicability explicit.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations concerning fixed sparsity scheduling and frozen reference supervision. Figure 6 motivates concern about skipping important tokens, while the conclusion proposes adaptive retention schedules and the limitations suggest stronger teacher guidance. The earlier capacity-matching interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2's promise of a future code/model release is replaced by a project-site link in v3's header. The PDFs do not establish whether linked resources are available. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, caching instructions, and decoder implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: The VideoPASTA citation and bibliography entry, reference 23 in v2, are removed. Positioning relative to RHO-1, LaVi, LLaVA-Meteor, and distillation methods remains substantively unchanged; most other reference edits concern style and metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, integrates supplementary decoder explanations into Section 3.4, expands the conclusion, and adds Limitations and Acknowledgments. It also adopts author-year citations and lettered appendices, while preserving most of the narrative and main section sequence.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout with different page dimensions, margins, typography, column widths, and figure/table scaling. Algorithm 1 moves into the main method section, and a full-page Figure 6 is added. Existing Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–9 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves visibility of the decoder implementation and adds useful limitations, but its main new analysis contains unresolved inconsistencies. Figure 6 calls NASA skipped despite marking it retained, and its summed losses do not explain the stated lambda=0.5 weighting. With the benchmark evidence unchanged, these problems undermine the added analysis enough that a reliable net quality improvement is unclear.
